User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the BriqueBoost application.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

Item.title: Item
Item.description: Represents an item that a user has purchased for resale.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this item. (Relationship: User 1:N Item)

purchasePrice.description: The price the user paid for the item.

purchaseDate.description: The date the user purchased the item.

condition.description: The condition of the item when purchased.

source.description: The source from which the item was purchased (e.g., thrift store, online marketplace).

notes.description: Any additional notes about the item.

Listing.title: Listing
Listing.description: Represents an enhanced product listing for an item.

itemId.description: Reference to the Item this listing is for. (Relationship: Item 1:1 Listing)

title.description: The enhanced title generated for the item.

description.description: The enhanced description generated for the item.

reasoning.description: The AI's reasoning for the generated title and description.

listingPrice.description: The price at which the item is listed for sale.

platform.description: The sales platform the item is listed on (e.g., eBay, Etsy).

status.description: The current status of the listing (e.g., active, sold, draft).

Sale.title: Sale
Sale.description: Represents a sale of an item.

listingId.description: Reference to the Listing that was sold. (Relationship: Listing 1:1 Sale)

salePrice.description: The price at which the item was sold.

saleDate.description: The date the item was sold.

profit.description: The profit made from the sale (salePrice - purchasePrice).

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to securely manage user data, items, listings, and sales for the BriqueBoost application. It prioritizes Authorization Independence by using path-based ownership for private user data and avoids hierarchical `get()` calls in security rules. Segregation is achieved by storing user-specific data under `/users/{userId}` paths, ensuring homogeneous security requirements within each collection.  This design facilitates straightforward and robust security rules while supporting atomic operations. Path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/items/{itemId}`) enables efficient and secure `list` operations for user-owned data, addressing the QAPs requirement.
